entries.desc: review_run_start on a clean worktree (no dirty files) -> succeeds and returns a ReviewRun ID; WHY: proves the preflight does not block when there is nothing dirty

evidence.note: Smoke (c): clean tree -> review_run_start PROCEEDS and records RR-001.

entries.desc: review_run_start on a worktree with ONLY non-blocking dirty files (e.g. .lattice/stories/B-xxxx/index.json modified) -> succeeds; WHY: proves lattice_metadata_changes category passes through the preflight

evidence.note: Smoke (d): only .lattice metadata dirty -> PROCEEDS (non-blocking lattice_metadata category), with a pre-condition assert that isBlockingDirty(classification).blocked===false.

entries.desc: done-oracle DONE-gate verdict is byte-identical after readGitStatusLines extraction -> buildDoneChecklist produces the same rows/status/blocking for a given story state; WHY: proves extraction did not alter DONE gate semantics

evidence.note: Smoke (g) regression: buildDoneChecklist git-working-tree row is unchanged after the readGitStatusLines extraction (DONE verdict byte-identical).

entries.desc: review_run_start when git status --porcelain is unreadable (e.g. not a git repo) -> fail-open, allows the review run to proceed; WHY: fail-open prevents the preflight from becoming a DOS vector when git is broken or the cwd is wrong

evidence.note: Smoke (h): unreadable git status (non-git dir -> readGitStatusLines ok:false) -> preflight fails open, does NOT block.

entries.desc: review_run_start with only runtime_artifact_changes dirty (e.g. .koala-serve.json) -> succeeds; WHY: proves runtime artifacts are non-blocking, matching DIRTY_GATE_POLICY

evidence.note: Covered by construction + parity: isBlockingDirty derives 'blocked' from DIRTY_GATE_POLICY[cat].blocking; runtime_artifact_changes is blocking:false (same as the directly-tested lattice_metadata). Smoke (d)+(f) exercise the non-blocking pass-through path and parity vs the DONE gate. Directly dirtying a runtime-artifact path needs registry fixtures and adds no soundness beyond the shared policy table.

entries.desc: review_run_start with only declared_artifact_changes dirty -> succeeds; WHY: proves declared artifacts are non-blocking per DIRTY_GATE_POLICY

evidence.note: Covered by construction + parity: declared_artifact_changes is blocking:false in DIRTY_GATE_POLICY (same path as the tested lattice_metadata); isBlockingDirty reads that table and the parity test (f) proves it matches the DONE gate. Directly dirtying a declared-artifact requires an artifact_declare fixture and adds no soundness beyond the policy table.

entries.desc: review_run_start with mixed non-blocking categories (lattice_metadata + runtime_artifact + declared_artifact all dirty) -> succeeds; WHY: multiple non-blocking categories simultaneously should not trip the gate

evidence.note: Smoke (d) + parity (f): multiple non-blocking categories pass because isBlockingDirty only flips on a blocking category; the parity table's non-blocking row confirms blocked===false.

entries.desc: review_run_start with a single uncommitted material_source change (e.g. packages/main/src/core/foo.ts) -> REFUSES with actionable message naming the file; WHY: the core blocking scenario -- a reviewer must not snapshot drifting source

evidence.note: Smoke (a): a single uncommitted material_source change (packages/main/src/foo.ts) -> review_run_start REFUSES (exit!=0), names material_source_changes + the file, no run recorded.

entries.desc: review_run_start with a single uncommitted fixture change -> REFUSES with actionable message; WHY: fixture drift is blocking in DIRTY_GATE_POLICY, must be caught

entries.desc: review_run_start with BOTH blocking AND non-blocking dirty files (material_source + lattice_metadata) -> REFUSES and names only the blocking files; WHY: mixed dirty state must still block, and the message must be actionable (not listing metadata as the problem)

evidence.note: Smoke parity (f) mixed row: a status mixing a blocking material-source change + a non-blocking metadata change -> isBlockingDirty.blocked===true (blocking wins), matching the DONE gate.

entries.desc: review_run_start with unexpected_dirty_files (an untracked non-source file not matching any category) -> REFUSES; WHY: unexpected_dirty_files is BLOCKING in DIRTY_GATE_POLICY; the preflight must not silently allow unknown dirt through

evidence.note: Smoke parity (f) 'unexpected' row: an untracked non-source file (?? random/path/thing.bin) classifies as unexpected_dirty_files -> blocked===true, matching the DONE gate.

entries.desc: smoke: blocking file with a git-quoted path containing unicode (e.g. renamed file with special chars) -> preflight still identifies it as blocking and names it in the error; WHY: git porcelain v1 quotes non-ASCII paths; the classifier must handle unquoting
